_comment: LINK-ONLY index of Yamato Security detection content, keyed by ATT&CK technique. Per technique and rule repo: the rule count, up to per_technique_refs rule refs (critical/high first, then by path) and, when there are more, `dirs` — every directory holding that technique's rules with its count (link = the source's tree_url + dir). Rule refs carry metadata only, never detection logic; `author` is verbatim (the DRL 1.1 attribution). Every Sigma document with an id is a rule: a correlation file's correlation rule and each of its base rules are separate refs (kind correlation / base) with the same path and URL; a correlation inherits no ATT&CK tag from its base rules. Rules with no ATT&CK tag are counted under sources.<repo>.untagged by product/service/category. Every indexed rule's Sigma id is in sources.<repo>.rule_ids, so any of them is a valid hunt_package_ref. Senrigan hunts (AGPL-3.0: CloudTrail, Suzaku timeline and VPC Flow Log hunts) are listed in senrigan_hunts with ids derived from their names and the telemetry they read (cloudtrail/<eventSource>, vpcflow/<required column>); techniques.<T>.senrigan lists the hunt ids (AWS Threat Technique Catalog ids such as T1562.A001 file under their ATT&CK parent). The consumer runs Hayabusa / Takajo / Suzaku / Senrigan on their own logs (workflows/wf-threat-analyst.md Phase 5). Generated by intel_engine/IntelAnalysis/scripts/build_yamato_index.py — do not hand-edit.
